title: Enterprise Onboarding + Integration + Escalation + Health/QBR Playbook
author: Alex Chen
content:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates the standard operating procedures used by Redwood Inference Customer Success (CS) and Support for enterprise onboarding, integrations, escalation handling, ongoing health checks, and Quarterly Business Review (QBR) preparation. It is intended for CSMs, Solutions Engineers, Support Engineers, and SRE partners and provides a single-source reference for common workflows, SLAs, templates, and runbooks.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to all enterprise customers (Dedicated & Private deployments, and high-usage Hosted customers with enterprise contracts).
- Covers initial onboarding (0–90 days), integration checklist, incident/escalation escalation flow, known issues & workarounds, ongoing health monitoring, and QBR preparation.

Owners and escalation contacts:
- Playbook owner: Alex Chen (Customer Success) – alex.chen@redwood.ai
- Primary escalation owner (Support): Jordan Lee – jordan.lee@redwood.ai
- SRE escalation contact: Riley Morgan – riley.morgan@redwood.ai
- On-call (Support): see internal rota at /confluence/eng-sre/oncall-rotations

Onboarding checklist (timeline & deliverables):
Pre-onboarding (before kickoff):
1. Contract & SOW validated by Finance/Legal. Confirm: billing contact, SLA terms, data residency requirements.
2. Technical prerequisites validated: network IP allowlist, DNS entries, KMS/HSM requirements. Provide customer with integration checklist (see section below).
3. Provisioning: Dedicated pool reserved or Private deployment build scheduled; collect cluster capacity requirements (GPU type, min/max concurrency).

Day 0 (Kickoff):
1. Introductions: CSM, SE, Support L1 lead, SRE POC.
2. Review scope, SLOs, and timelines.
3. Share access: staging API keys, instance dashboard, runbook links.

Week 1 (Initial integration):
- Verify API connectivity: health check endpoint responds 200 within 250ms from customer region.
- Integration tests: sample generation, embeddings, streaming flows, and function-calling paths.
- Performance baseline: sample latency (p50/p95/p99), token cost estimate.

Week 2–4 (Stabilization):
- Tune retry/backoff and batching recommendations.
- Turn on prefix/KV caching for common workloads if applicable.
- Schedule canary traffic if migrating production workloads.

90-day handoff:
- Finalize playbook: runbook links, escalation contacts, billing/usage review.
- Move to standard support coverage and QBR cadence.

Integration checklist (technical):
- Network & connectivity:
  - IP ranges to allow: 34.198.0.0/16, 52.23.128.0/17 (provide up-to-date list from infra).
  - TLS: TLS 1.2+ enforced.
  - Firewall: outbound ports 443 allowed to *.redwood-inference.internal (use customer-specific endpoints provided in provisioning email).
- Authentication:
  - API keys for initial integration (rotate to mTLS/JWT if required by security).
  - For Private: KMS integration checklist (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / HSM) – include key alias and IAM role.
- Webhooks & callbacks:
  - Ensure public callback URL and signed payload verification using HMAC-SHA256.
- Monitoring & observability:
  - Provide Prometheus scrape endpoint (if Private) or configure log forwarding (syslog/CloudWatch).
  - Request that customer share representative traffic samples (anonymized) for perf tuning.
- Compliance & data handling:
  - Confirm data residency and retention policy.
  - If regulated: enable audit-logging and preserve logs for 90–365 days per contract.

Sample integration acceptance tests (to run with customer):
1. API auth: call /v1/health with provided key -> expect {status: "ok"} and latency < 300ms.
2. Generation: send 1k token prompt -> check throughput and token cost estimate matches projection.
3. Streaming: start streaming response and confirm headers/support for chunked transfer.
4. Embeddings: compute 100 vectors < 2000 dims; verify average latency.

Escalation playbook (severity definitions and steps):
Severity mapping:
- Sev1 (Critical): Production outage impacting all users or >50% of requests failing; immediate business impact. Target RTT: 15 minutes.
- Sev2 (High): Degraded performance with major feature impact (e.g., p95 latency spike > 3x baseline). Target RTT: 1 hour.
- Sev3 (Medium): Functional issues affecting a subset of users or non-blocking regressions. Target RTT: 4 business hours.
- Sev4 (Low): Cosmetic or minor issues, feature requests, or onboarding questions. Target RTT: 2 business days.

Escalation steps (ordered):
1. Triage (Support L1) – confirm reproducible steps, gather logs, customer env, sample requests. Document in ticket.
2. If Sev1/Sev2 or unknown root cause -> escalate to Support L2 + CSM + SRE.
3. SRE runbook activation for runtime incidents (see eng-sre/runbooks/incident-response).
4. Executive escalation: If incident exceeds SLA window (see contract) or customer requests, notify Director of Support and Customer Success.

Communication templates (initial incident):
- Subject: [SEV1] {Customer} – {Short summary}
- Body: 1) Impact summary and ETA; 2) Actions taken; 3) Next update cadence (every 30 minutes for Sev1).

Post-incident:
- Run RCA: SRE + Support + CS present within 72 hours.
- Share a joint customer-facing postmortem within 5 business days, unless contract requires an executive-level report.

Support process & ticket flow:
- Channels accepted: Support portal (primary), email enterprise-support@redwood.ai (backup), and dedicated Slack channel (if provisioned).
- Ticket routing: automatic triage based on keywords & SLA (Support L1 -> L2 -> SRE).
- Escalation SLA obligations:
  - Sev1: acknowledge in 15 minutes, update every 30 minutes, restore/mitigate within SLA window per contract.
  - Sev2: acknowledge in 1 hour, update every 2 hours.
  - Sev3: acknowledge 4 business hours.
  - Sev4: acknowledge 2 business days.

Ticket metadata required on handoff:
- Customer name, environment (staging/prod), region, API key id, sample request IDs, timestamps, p50/p95 latency from last 1 hour, and any relevant logs.

Known issues and common workarounds (triage-ready):
1. Issue: Intermittent 504s from the gateway when KV cache is warm.
   - Symptoms: 5xxs concentrated during bursts; error rate spikes to 2–3%.
   - Mitigation: Increase gateway worker pool, enable graceful queuing, and temporarily enable smaller batching. Action owner: Eng-Serving-Runtime.
2. Issue: Embeddings dimensionality mismatch on customer model adapter.
   - Symptoms: Client errors with "vector shape mismatch".
   - Workaround: Normalize to expected dim in client; deploy adapter patch v1.2.1.
3. Issue: Slow p95 for streaming responses on older GPUs (A100->T4 migration case).
   - Symptoms: p95 latency increase by 2x for long-context prompts.
   - Mitigation: Pin model variant with quantization profile Q2 and enable KV cache persistence.

Health checks and operational metrics (dashboards & alerts):
- Core metrics to track (minimum):
  - Requests per minute (RPM) by customer and model.
  - Error rate (5xx) by customer (alert if >0.5% sustained for 5m).
  - Latency p50/p95/p99 (alert if p95 > 3x baseline for 10m).
  - Token throughput and estimated cost per 1k tokens.
  - Queue length and rejected requests (alert if queue depth > 1000).
- Suggested alerts:
  - Sev2: p95 latency > 500ms for Hosted enterprise endpoints for 10m.
  - Sev1: 5xx > 2% sustained for 5m or system-wide rate limiting engaged.
- Dashboard widgets (example):
  - Customer overview: daily RPM, error rate, costs (7d trend).
  - Model performance: p50/p95/p99 latency heatmap by model.
  - Capacity: GPU utilization, free slot counts, scheduled maintenance windows.

Quarterly Business Review (QBR) template and cadence:
- Cadence: Quarterly for enterprise customers, or monthly for top-tier accounts.
- Attendees: CSM, Customer POC, Solutions Engineer, Support Manager, (optional) VP Customer Success.
- Agenda (standard 60–90 min):
  1. Welcome and goals (5m)
  2. Health snapshot: uptime, error rate, latency, usage & cost trends (10–15m)
  3. Business impact and wins: feature launches, latency improvements, cost reductions (10–15m)
  4. Roadmap alignment: upcoming product features, migration plans (15m)
  5. Risks & escalations: open tickets > Sev2, pending capacity/contract issues (10m)
  6. Action items and next steps (5–10m)
- Deliverables after QBR: share slide deck, updated action item tracker, schedule next QBR.

QBR success metrics (examples):
- Achievement of latency SLOs (p95 < contract threshold) across 90-day window.
- Reduction in mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for Sev1 incidents to < 10 minutes.
- Cost per 1M tokens improved vs baseline by at least 5% through batching/caching changes.

Documentation and runbooks (references):
- eng-sre/runbooks/incident-response (SRE runbook)
- eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite (performance tuning)
- eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides (private deployment checklist)
- product-docs/roadmap-and-themes (feature timelines)

Appendix: quick checklists and templates
- Pre-kickoff email template: includes API endpoints, test API key, integration checklist, and pre-kickoff form for customer to complete.
- Post-incident update cadence template: timeline and recipients for Sev1, Sev2.

Change log:
- 2026-09-15: Consolidated QBR templates and added health dashboard widget recommendations. Updated IP ranges note to reference infra canonical list.
- 2025-08-01: Initial playbook authored.

If anything in this playbook conflicts with an individual customer contract or security requirement, follow the contract and notify Legal + Security. For updates to this document, contact the playbook owner.
